NOTE_TEXT: 84d s/p lumbar laminectomy. Caregiver called for f/u. Pt unable to identify which sx warrant ED evaluation or urgent call to surgeon. Discussed red flags including increased leg weakness, loss of bowel/bladder control, fever, worsening numbness. Caregiver verbalized understanding; will monitor and call with concerns.

Pt called with c/o persistent nausea x 3 days. Denies food intolerance or diarrhea. States started after d/c, not better w/ ginger ale or small meals. Thought it might be from anesthesia lingering but pt also ate different lunch yesterday. Denies abd pain or fever. VM left w/ RN re: possible post-op nausea, ROV if worsens or vomits.

Pt called today 52d s/p colectomy. C/o persistent pain throughout abdomen, states taking all prescribed meds as directed but still having significant discomfort. Denies localized incision pain, pain appears diffuse. Encouraged pt to contact surgeon's office given ongoing symptoms despite compliance w/ regimen. Will attempt VM to surgeon's office for urgent follow-up.

Pt called with concern re: chest tube site, states it has been weeping serosanguinous drainage x 2 days s/p CABG. Denies fever or increased pain. VM to cardiothoracic surgery clinic for assessment. Pt instructed to keep site clean and dry, monitor for increased output or signs of infection. ROV pending surgical eval.
POC call to pt s/p discharge, reports confusion re: wound care & dressing changes, states doesn't know what to do. Instructed pt on technique, will call back tomorrow to confirm understanding.

Pt called in, 13d post-d/c. Reports having trouble figuring out how to use the CPAP machine at night, not sure if he's doing it right. Also having difficulty managing the walker around the house, particularly with turns. Denies falls but states he's uncomfortable moving around independently. VM left for RN to follow up w/ equipment company and consider PT eval.

Called pt at 0930, VM left requesting callback at earliest convenience re: post-d/c follow-up. ROV today if possible. Pt called back around 1145, doing ok overall, says weather has been nice so been getting out a bit which is good for morale. Mentioned daughter visiting from out of state this weekend. When asked about the new med we discussed before discharge pt became a bit uncertain, says they dont think they ever got it filled, checked at their pharmacy yesterday and the pharmacy tech said nothing was on file for them, pt not sure if we sent it or if there was some miscommunication. Went back through discharge paperwork pt has at home and cant locate the script, pt says maybe it didnt get sent from the hospital or maybe they lost it. Also c/o some persistent lower back pain but denies its related to recent hospitalization. Pt denies any f/c, chest pain, SOB. Will send new script today from our end and confirm receipt directly w/ pharmacy. Pt agreeable, will expect to hear back from them soon. Advised to call if any concerns arise in interim.

Caregiver called POD#2 re pt c/o dark black stools x1 this AM; denies further episodes, denies abd pain or lightheadedness, tolerating diet. Advised to monitor and call back if recurs or any vomiting of blood.

Initial VM left at 1400, pt to call back when available Pt called back this afternoon, c/o frequent loose stools x 3 days since discharge. States 4-5 times daily, no blood, no fever. Recently started antibiotics during hosp stay, aware meds can cause this. Denies abd pain or cramping. Tolerating POs, drinking fluids. Advised to call if worsens or develops fever/severe cramping. Continue current diet, monitor stools.

Pt called w/ c/o nausea x 3 wks, denies relation to appendectomy 54d ago. Denies vomiting, appetite fair, tolerating POs. Worsens in AM, improves w/ food. Denies fever, abd pain, change in BMs. Reports new stress at work x 6 wks. Advised to f/u w/ PCP for eval, given timing doesn't align w/ surgical recovery. VM left on chart.

Pt called to report dark tarry stools x 2-3 days, denies abdominal pain or n/v. 41d s/p lumbar laminectomy, denies current GI meds or NSAIDs. Advised pt to seek ED evaluation today, instructed to call 911 if hematemesis or severe abdominal pain develops. Pt voiced understanding and agreed to go to ED. VM sent to PCP for awareness.

Pt called today, 2d s/p d/c. States has been noticing her heart doing funny things, says it feels like it's racing and then skips and races again, happens off and on. Denies CP but says she's feeling it a lot, maybe 5-6x since she got home. Tried to watch her granddaughter yesterday, had to sit down because of it. Mentioned her daughter is making her lunches now which is nice, though the weather has been so hot the fridge has been working overtime. Pt says she's taking her meds as prescribed, all the pills in the little organizer. Denies SOB but notes the palpitations make her anxious. Asked if she needs to do anything about it or just wait it out. Advised to call MD if worsens or if develops CP, SOB, or dizziness; can also call back to speak w/ RN. Will have VM from office reach out as well. Pt verbalized understanding.

called pt residence at 1400, no answer, VM left requesting call back regarding post-d/c f/u spoke w/ daughter at 1530. pt doing OK at home, denies fever/chills/SOB. states has not heard back about lab work ordered before discharge 8d ago and unclear what results mean or if needs further action. daughter concerned, trying to reach DC provider. advised to have pt or daughter contact lab directly for results, will attempt contact to DC team today. ROV plan discussed, no acute c/o at this time
Pt called reporting episodes of feeling lightheaded and dizzy over past 2 wks, denies falls but had one near-miss yesterday morning when standing from bed. Denies LOC, c/o no chest pain or SOB.

Pt called today 17d s/p lap chole, c/o concern abt JP drain. States drain output has changed to greenish color over past 2-3d and amt seems less than initial wks. Denies fever, abd pain, or signs of infection. Instructed to observe drain closely and VM surg office if output changes further or if develops redness/warmth around site. Pt verbalized understanding.

Pt called today 71d s/p TKA. States difficulty obtaining foods that fit w/ prescribed diet at local market. Denies understanding what foods allowed vs not. Lives alone, unable to travel farther for specialty grocery. Discussed options for delivery services & meal prep resources. VM left w/ dietary dept for follow-up.

Pt called today POD 14. C/o continued pain despite adhering to prescribed pain regimen. States pain is generalized, denies localization to incision site. Pain not improving w/ current meds taken as directed. Pt reports following all post-d/c instructions. Advised to contact surgeon if pain worsens or does not improve in next 24-48 hrs. VM left for MD callback.

POD 12 f/u call, pt reached directly. Reports current living situation at daughter's apartment - states heat not working in unit, temp dropping at night. Daughter working long hrs, pt alone most of day. Denies falls but c/o difficulty navigating stairs in dim lighting. Discussed concerns re: safety w pt, advised to contact daughter re: repairs and daylight alternatives. Will f/u in 2 days to check on resolution.

Called pt at 1430, no answer. VM left requesting pt call back at convenience. Pt called back at 1615. Speaking w pt who states doing ok overall, weather has been nice where she is, been able to get outside a bit. Mentioned daughter visiting next month which she's looking forward to. Asked about surgical site and pt reports incision looks ok but expressed confusion about dressing changes - stated unsure if supposed to change it herself or when to change it or what to use. Went over instructions pt received at discharge per chart but pt admits didn't really understand them at the time, said everything was a blur after surgery. Explained step by step how to assess for signs of drainage, when dressing needs changing, what supplies to use. Pt asking good questions now - seemed to grasp it better w verbal walk through. Also mentioned some lower back pain unrelated which she takes tylenol for but denies any fever, chills, or increased redness/warmth around incision. Instructed pt to call if any concerns arise before next follow up w surgeon. Will send written instructions via mail as well given pt's initial confusion w discharge materials.

Pt called in, VM left on first attempt at 10:15a asking him to ROV. Pt called back at 1430. Pt reports doing ok overall but having some trouble with his breathing lately, says he gets short of breath just going up the stairs or even sitting around watching tv which is new for him since he came home 2 weeks ago. Says his wife keeps bugging him about it, she thinks he should come back in. Mentioned the weather has been humid and that always bothers him anyway but this feels different he says. Also complained about his knees hurting from the humidity which he knows is unrelated but thought I should know. When asked about chest pain he denies, no fevers, no cough. Pt states he takes his meds as prescribed including the new one we discussed. Lives with wife, adult daughter visiting from out of state actually arriving tomorrow. Pt wondering if maybe he is just deconditioned from being in hospital but concerned because it is getting worse not better. Encouraged pt to follow up with PCP within next few days and to go to ED if worsening or develops chest pain. Pt states will call PCP tomorrow and will VM if needs anything else.
Pt called re: script from surgeon not filled yet, pharmacy says insurance needs approval first. States has been waiting, needs refill soon.

pt called today, 10d s/p d/c. doing ok overall but mentioned something that started about 3-4 days ago - hands are all tingly and kinda numb especially at night when hes trying to sleep. says it wakes him up sometimes. wife asked if it could b related to the new BP med started before he left hosp, metoprolol i think, and honestly pt seemed to think that made sense. denies any recent falls or injuries, temp sensation intact per pt report. also complained a bunch abt the weather been too hot and his garden is dying, asked if i knew anything abt that which i dont. mentioned he tried the new blood pressure med consistently as directed. denies chest pain, denies SOB. we talked abt his kids for a minute - theyre visiting next month apparently. told him to call his PCP monday before he takes another dose and to keep track if the numbness gets worse or changes. VM left for his cardio to call back when they get a chance. otherwise wound healing well, no signs of infection, tolerating diet fine

Pt's daughter called to report that incision site continues to have significant pain 12d s/p lumbar laminectomy. States pain not adequately controlled on current Rx regimen. Denies fever, drainage, or redness. Pt tolerating POs and ambulating w/ walker. Advised to contact surgeon's office for possible adjustment to pain meds or VM to physician.
Pt called, c/o unable to fill new Rx due to cost - states copay too high, unclear if already filled and rationing or has not started yet.

Attempted contact 1400h, no answer. VM left requesting pt callback at earliest convenience re: post-op f/u. Pt called back 1430h. States doing okay overall, wound is bothering her though. Says the incision on her belly where the surgery was is looking pretty red around the edges and feels warm to touch. She mentioned there's some drainage coming out, says it's yellowish and kinda gross looking, not just clear like it was right after the surgery. Asked how long this has been going on and she said maybe 3-4 days now, wasn't like this when she first got home. We talked about the weather for a minute, she was complaining about how hot it's been, making it hard to keep the area clean and dry. Also mentioned her daughter is visiting from out of town next week which is exciting. Reviewed signs to watch for - increasing redness, fever, spreading warmth. Pt denies fever, denies severe pain but does say the area is tender. Instructed to monitor closely, keep area clean and dry, call back immediately if worsens or develops fever. Advised ROV with PCP if not improving in next 2-3 days. Pt verbalized understanding. Will follow up in 24h.

Pt called to check in POD#4. States has rx in hand but hasn't started taking yet, unsure about directions. Not clear if pt didn't receive from pharmacy or holding off on initiation. VM ROV with patient regarding instructions and will follow up in 48hrs to confirm started.

Called pt at 0930, no answer. VM left requesting callback at earliest convenience re: post-op f/u. Caregiver called back 1400. Pt doing well recovery-wise, denies c/c, incision healing fine. Caregiver reports pt needs PT s/p CABG but cannot afford the copay for outpatient sessions—insurance req $50/session and pt states would need ~12 wks of tx, unable to manage cost. Discussed sliding scale at cardiac rehab center, provided contact info. Pt to call back PRN w/ questions.

Called by daughter on POD#11 s/p discharge. Pt c/o heart racing and skipping beats x 3 days, denies CP or SOB. Noticing it mostly when lying down at night. Denies fever, takes metoprolol as prescribed. Instructed to call MD if worsens or develops chest pain, ROV if unable to reach PCP by EOB tomorrow.

Pt called post-op day 53 s/p lumbar laminectomy. Denies pain, incision healing well, tolerating activity as tolerated. States has not rec'd any follow-up appt yet and unsure who to contact. Advised to call surgeon's office tomorrow to schedule post-op eval. Also noted duplicate chart exists in system - flagged for medical records to consolidate prior to next visit.

Spoke w/ daughter re pt s/p hernia repair 15d ago. Reports drain site has been oozing more than usual past 3d, yellowish fluid, pt c/o mild tenderness around drain area. Daughter asking when drain should be removed, states pt reluctant to move around much due to discomfort. Instructed to monitor for increased drainage, fever, or sign of infection. VM left for surgical team re drain management.

Pt called c/o fever and chills since yesterday, temp spikes to 101.8, feeling achy. Also questioned whether insurance will cover the compression garment ordered at discharge. Advised to contact ins co directly for coverage determination, provided member services number. Pt instructed to call back if temp rises or symptoms worsen. Reassured about typical post-d/c follow-up but noted concern given fever onset timeline, suggested contacting PCP if not improving.

Pt called requesting clarification on wound care. States unsure how to change dressing, asking if it should be removed daily or left in place. Denies having received written instructions at discharge, unsure of frequency for dressing changes and what supplies to use. RN reviewed dressing change procedure verbally and instructed pt to call with any further questions.

Pt called for post-d/c f/u 2 days s/p discharge. Denies any acute c/c at this time, tolerating diet and ambulating independently. Reports having received 2 separate discharge summaries in mail from same hospitalization and unsure which one is current; pt confused about the discrepancy. Advised pt to retain both documents and bring to next PCP visit for clarification. Pt agreeable, no further concerns VM'd.

Pt called to f/u post-colectomy s/p discharge 68d. C/o nausea x 1-2wks, denies association w/ meals or po intake. Vomiting 2-3x/wk, non-bloody. Denies fever, abd pain, or changes in bowel habits. Instructed to contact PCP if symptoms worsen or if unable to maintain oral intake. VM left w/ contact number for ROV as needed.

Called pt's daughter this AM to check in on how he's doing post-op, she said he's managing okay overall but weather's been crazy lately hasn't it, anyway he's still got the incision bandaged but she had no idea how often to change it or really what to look for when she does. Said she didn't want to mess with it wrong and make something worse. We went over the basics – when to change, what supplies he needs, what kind of drainage is normal versus concerning. She wrote down the instructions we went through but seemed a little overwhelmed honestly, I told her to call back if anything looks off or if they just aren't sure. Pt denies fever, denies unusual pain beyond normal incision soreness, ambulating well s/p appendectomy 70 days ago, wound appears to be healing though he's been cautious about letting anyone look at it. Daughter will call VM if questions come up. Encouraged daily gentle cleaning and to keep area dry, gave her surgeon's number to ROV dressing supplies if needed.

VM left 0945 - pt not available, requested call back this PM Pt reached. Wound drain d/c'd pre-discharge, pt states unclear abt how to actually change the dressing daily & unsure abt what to look for w/ the incision. Denies s/s of infection. Reviewed step-by-step process during call & pt able to teach-back appropriately. Instructed to contact surgeon office w/ any q's PRN. Pt comfortable proceeding.

Pt called re: post-op s/p cholecystectomy, 7wks ago. Reports confusion—surgeon said OK to resume normal diet but NP said to avoid fatty foods. Wants clarification on diet restrictions. VM left w/ surgeon's office for ROV.

Pt called reporting feeling light-headed and dizzy since d/c, had one episode yesterday where nearly fell getting out of bed. Denies chest pain or SOB. Instructed on slow position changes, encouraged increased fluids, advised VM if persists or worsens.

Pt called in for post-d/c f/u s/p hysterectomy. Doing well overall, incision healing nicely per pt report, mild soreness around the area but manageable. Denies fever, chills, drainage or any acute c/o at this time. Weather has been nice so got out for a short walk yesterday which felt good. Mentioned daughter is visiting next month which she's looking forward to. Discussed current meds and pt states she has the script for the pain med but hasn't actually started taking it yet, says she's managing with just Tylenol and not sure she needs it. Encouraged her to follow prescribed regimen as written and explained this is important for first weeks post-op. Pt will think about it. Also c/o of some persistent lower back pain unrelated to surgery, been bothering her for years really. Said husband's been having GI issues too but that's his problem to sort. PT will f/u with prescribing dr regarding med adherence if she has Q's, available PRN. ROV 4-6 weeks or sooner if any concerns arise.

Pt called from home today doing well overall, c/o occasional chest pressure with exertion which pt states is improving, denies SOB at rest. Wound at incision site healing nicely per pt, no drainage or erythema noted on recent self-exam. Weather been nice lately so pt has been getting out more, mentioned grandkids visiting next month which he's looking forward to. Also mentioned some knee pain from old arthritis acting up but unrelated to surgery. When asked about wound care pt said "oh yeah the nurse showed me how to clean it before I left" and states he's been doing dressing changes as instructed s/p discharge. However when pressed pt admits he ran out of sterile gauze and saline about 3 wks ago and just been using regular bandages from the drugstore, stated he was waiting for the home care setup to get scheduled but hasn't heard anything yet and wasn't sure who to call about getting the supplies delivered. Denies any signs of infection but pt clearly needs arrangement for supplies and wound care visits to be established. Pt receptive to follow-up and said he can do whatever needs to happen.
Pt called reporting pressure in chest x2 days, intermittent, denies SOB/diaphoresis, pain 4/10, taking ASA PRN. Advised ROV ED if worsens or new sx; pt agreeable, will monitor.

POD#14 f/u call, pt called in c/o new tremor in hands since started on new beta blocker 5d ago, denies other side effects. Also reports nausea x3d, worse in AM, no vomiting, denies any relation to recent surgery. Denies fever, abd pain, recent dietary changes. Advised to call PCP re: tremor, encouraged oral fluids for nausea, VM left for pharmacy callback re: med review. ROV w/ PCP in 3d.

Called pt at 1400, no answer. VM left requesting return call, pt to call back when available. Pt called back at 1630. Reports ongoing nausea x 2 days, worse in AM, denies vomiting. Started post-op day 10 s/p CABG. Denies fever, abdominal pain, change in bowel function. Attributes to anesthesia/surgery. Advised to try small frequent meals, ginger tea, contact MD if worsens or if vomiting develops. Pt verbalized understanding, stated will reach out if issues persist.

Attempted post-d/c f/u call 56d s/p hysterectomy. Caregiver answered, stated pt not available at this number. Caregiver c/o number on file disconnected or incorrect - unable to reach pt directly to assess post-op status. Instructed caregiver to have pt contact clinic to update contact info and reschedule f/u call. No s/s of complications discussed due to inability to reach pt.

Attempted contact at 1400, no answer. VM left requesting pt call back at convenience. Pt called back 1630. POD#7 s/p appendectomy. C/o pain at incision site, describes as sharp, worse with movement. States current regimen (acetaminophen q6h, ibuprofen PRN) not adequate for relief. Denies fever, drainage, or redness at site. Instructed pt to contact surgeon's office tomorrow for evaluation, reviewed s/s that would warrant ED visit. Will follow up with pt in 2 days.

VM left 1145a re post-op follow up s/p cholecystectomy 3wks ago, pt to ROV Pt called back at 1430. C/o right upper quadrant tenderness at surgical site, states pain level 7/10 even after taking prescribed Norco PRN q4-6h x 2-3 doses daily. Denies fever, n/v, or changes in bowel function. Incision appears to be healing per pt report, no signs of infection noted. Discussed pain management options, advised to call surgeon's office given inadequate relief w/ current regimen and need to r/o post-op complication.

Pt answered. Advised of post-op f/u call regarding hernia repair recovery. Pt stated does not wish to participate in follow-up calls and requested to be removed from program. VM left 9/18 requesting call back re: post-discharge f/u. Pt called back this date. Pt c/o no acute issues but declines further contact. Requested removal from f/u protocol.

VM left at 1430, pt's caregiver CB requested call back today. ROV. Spoke w/ pt's daughter at 1645. Pt 87d s/p appendectomy, reports doing well, tolerating PO, no pain c/o, incision healing appropriately per pt report. Denies fever, nausea, or abnormal drainage. Daughter states pt ambulating and sleeping ok. No questions or concerns raised. Reassured re: activity progression and PRN analgesic use. Will f/u PRN.

PT called today, answered on 2nd attempt. 93d post-op s/p hysterectomy. 85yo pt reports living situation unstable since D/C. Currently staying w/ family member in crowded apt, states has not been able to rest properly, no safe place to lie down during day, kept stairs to bed at night which difficult given surgical recovery. Denies fall but c/o difficulty ambulating safely in home. Concerned about prolonged recovery. Advised re: pt resources, discussed w/ social work ROV. Pt encouraged to contact case mgmt re: discharge plan revision.

Pt called 3d s/p D/C. Verified current status doing ok, no acute c/o. During call pt advised that phone number on file is incorrect, states cell changed since admission. Updated to new number in system. Pt also noted mailing address no longer current will be relocating next month, requested updated forms be sent to new address once confirmed. ROV with pt prior to EoC.

Called pt's caregiver 14d s/p d/c, caregiver reports pt c/o confusion about wound dressing changes & denies having received instructions on care, VM left per pt request for RN callback VM to provide wound care education.

Pt called today for post-d/c f/u 10d s/p d/c. Pt doing okay overall, denies fever or increased SOB. Got a laugh about the weather saying it's been brutal with the cold snap. Mentioned his daughter visited on wknd which was nice. Then brought up that things at home are pretty rough right now - roof's been leaking since the fall and landlord keeps saying he'll fix it but hasn't. Pt says the water damage is getting worse and there's black spots showing up on the ceiling in the BR. Also mentioned the heat isn't working properly, keeps going on and off, and he's been sleeping in the living room mostly bc it's warmer there. Said he's worried about the mold and doesn't feel right being in that environment given everything that just happened with his hospitalization. Discussed need to follow up w/ PCP and got VM confirming PT app for next wk. Strongly encouraged pt to reach out to social work team for resources and ROV done regarding safety concerns at home.

Pt called c/o incision opening up at site s/p colectomy 12d ago. States sutures appear to be pulling apart, sees small gap widening along lower aspect of surgical site. Denies drainage, fever, or increased pain at this time. Advised pt to notify surgeon emergently and instructed not to manipulate area. VM left w surgeon's office directing urgent eval.

Spoke w/ daughter who is primary caregiver, pt at home resting. She mentioned it's been pretty warm out there the last few days which has made things harder. Daughter noted that pt's legs are looking "puffy" especially around the ankles and feet, says he noticed his pants are fitting tighter around the waist and he's already up about 4-5 lbs since coming home 6 days ago. Checked in about the new diuretic prescription filled at discharge—daughter states they have it in the medicine cabinet but pt "hasn't gotten around to" starting it yet, was planning to wait until he felt a little better. Discussed importance of starting the med as ordered and to reweigh daily, also mentioned the leg swelling could be related to not being on the medication. Caregiver will encourage him to begin taking it today. Also mentioned daughter's son just got engaged which is exciting news, they're talking about a wedding next year. Reminded them to call back if swelling gets worse or if he develops any SOB. VM left w/ pt's wife to make sure he gets the message.

Pt c/o redness and warmth at lumbar incision site s/p laminectomy 14d ago. Reports weeping from wound with yellowish drainage noted today. Denies fever or chills but states area tender to touch. VM left for pt to contact surgeon urgently regarding wound appearance. ROV if drainage increases or pt develops fever.
Attempted post-d/c f/u call on pt s/p lumbar laminectomy 69d ago, age 85+. VM left requesting pt to call back at clinic to discuss how pt is doing and any concerns since discharge. No contact made.

Pt's daughter called. Pt s/p discharge 9d ago. Daughter c/o pt having trouble w/ home glucose monitoring - unable to get consistent readings from meter, unsure if readings are accurate when they do display. Denies pt on new meds or recent trauma to fingertips. Instructed daughter to check meter battery & contact manufacturer if issue persists, arranged VM to pt's PCP ROV.

Called pt's daughter who reports pt has been asking "where am I" repeatedly since yesterday morning & doesn't recognize family members visiting. Daughter states this is very different from baseline. Pt is oriented to person & name but not time or place. Denies fever, no falls noted, pt eating/drinking PO without difficulty. Advised daughter to contact PCP today & report findings; discussed bringing pt to ED if worsening or if unable to reach provider.

Attempted call at 1430, no answer. VM left requesting callback at pt convenience. Caregiver called back at 1645, states pt c/o sharp pain around incision site x 3 days, constant aching when not taking meds. Denies fever, nausea, drainage from wound. S/p appendectomy 20d ago, incision site looks clean per caregiver. Tried ibuprofen and acetaminophen alternating q4h but pain breaks thru, only gets relief with opioid. Denies pain elsewhere in abdomen. Advised caregiver to call surgeon ROV today given inadequate pain control at surgical site and to have wound reassessed in office.

Called pt residence at 0930, caregiver answered. Pt resting in bed at this time, vm left requesting callback within 24hrs Caregiver called back at 1145. States pt noticed feet and ankles are "puffier than usual" since coming home 3d ago. Caregiver reports pt's regular shoes no longer fit comfortably. Pt has gained approx 4-5 lbs per caregiver report. Denies new dyspnea, orthopnea, or SOB. No recent falls. Instructed caregiver to monitor for increasing swelling, check skin integrity, and notify MD if worsening or new symptoms develop. Pt to elevate legs when resting.

POV call d/c day 2. Pt c/o concern re: scheduling follow-up urology appt but states cannot afford copay at this time. Denies other issues s/p d/c. Instructed pt re: financial assistance options available through urology dept & encouraged to call office to discuss. VM left w/ number.
Pt called re: not filling colostomy supplies script - states rx never sent to pharmacy or not in system. Pt denies receiving, pharmacy has no record. Advised to contact surgeon's office to resubmit.

Called by daughter. Pt c/o continued oozing from surgical site on knee, denies fever. Daughter reports bruising around knee remains significant at 75d s/p surgery & asks if on coumadin causing bleed. Pt on warfarin for afib, INR due for check. VM left for PCP to address bleeding concern & verify INR status.

VM left requesting callback, no answer on initial attempt 1/15 11am Caregiver (daughter) reached on ROV. Pt doing well overall s/p TKA, knee ROM improving. Daughter reports pt got Rx filled at discharge but insurance only covering 1 month supply of pain med at copay pt could manage. 2nd month copay came much higher, so pt rationing tablets to extend supply rather than refill. Discussed options including contacting prescriber re: samples or lower-cost alternatives, and insurance formulary review.

Called pt's daughter this AM re f/u post hysterectomy, pt doing OK overall but reports she's been feeling pretty queasy since getting home 15 days ago, not really improving much. Daughter mentioned that pt had to leave work yesterday because she felt like she was gonna throw up but didn't actually get sick, just felt awful. I asked if there was anything specific that set it off - like certain foods - and daughter said no, it seems more constant, waves of it throughout the day especially when she first wakes up or after taking her pain meds. Mentioned the heat we've been having has her exhausted too but that's separate. She's keeping food down most of the time when she does eat but says even the smell of chicken makes her turn green which is weird because that's normally her favorite. Daughter thinks maybe it's lingering from the anesthesia since she had such a rough recovery room experience and was groggy for hours after waking up. I told her to keep monitoring and that some folks do have delayed nausea from surgery meds, and to call back if it gets worse or if she develops fever or abd distention.

POV c/o redness and warmth at sternotomy incision site, pt's daughter reports weeping and what appears to be pus drainage x since dc 3d ago s/p CABG. Denies fever, pt states area is tender. Advised to notify MD today, given wound concerns this early post-op. Contact made w/ daughter as primary caller, pt available in background.

Pt called today 55d s/p hysterectomy. Reports doing well overall, c/o mild residual achiness but manageable. When asked about monitoring, pt states not doing daily weights or BP checks as instructed. Pt acknowledges was given instructions at discharge but "just hasn't gotten around to it." Reinforced importance of monitoring per post-op plan, pt agrees to start today, will use home scale and cuff she has available. VM left with specific reminder to resume checks daily.

VM left on 1st attempt, pt called back approx 30 min later. Pt c/o trouble getting nebulizer mask on correctly, says it keeps leaking and mask seal feels loose. Also having difficulty setting up CPAP nightly - confused about tubing connections and denies anyone at home to help. Stated he usually gives up after 5-10 min of trying. Instructed on proper mask fitting technique, encouraged to call durable med equipment supplier for in-home setup assistance. Pt verbalized understanding. Will ROV in 3-5 days.

Pt called to report redness, warmth and purulent drainage from appendectomy incision site x 3 days. Denies fever, abd pain, or other s/s. Also c/o unable to reach surgeon's office, called 4 times since d/c d/19, VM left but no ROV. Tried PCP and specialist office same issue. Instructed pt to go to ED if drainage worsens or develops fever/chills. Contacted surgeon's office on pt's behalf, left urgent message re: incision concerns.

Called pt today 42d s/p hernia repair. Doing ok overall, says weather's been nice where he is. Mentioned his daughter just started college which is exciting. But when asked about incision and how recovery going, pt c/o that pain is not well controlled even though he's taking all his meds exactly as prescribed. Says it's not really at the incision site - more generalized, sorta aches all over. Denies fever, denies any drainage or redness at incision. Taking pain meds as directed but they're not touching it. Pt works construction so he's been trying to take it easy but says he's going stir crazy at home. Reiterated multiple times that the pain is persistent and not localized to where the surgery was done. VM left for covering MD to evaluate further - pt aware needs follow up.

POD#3 f/u call w/ caregiver. Pt unsure re: restrictions on lifting, driving, and activity level at home. Instructed to contact surgeon's office for clearance before resuming normal ADLs.
